top_choice_rationale: P001 awards optical lattice clocks to Katori and Ye alone. The magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct idea from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion control prizes: the trap shift cancels between the clock states, so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once. Independent laboratories (RIKEN/Tokyo, JILA, NIST, PTB, SYRTE) agree at the 10^-18 level, so maturity is established, and the two-name allocation is the one every supporter has converged on. I rank P002 second because it contains the same clock part, but its added IceCube part credits Halzen alone, a single-name credit for a large collaboration that I cannot judge from my own field and that the committee has not resolved. P003 (cold-atom quantum simulation, Bloch, Greiner, Zoller) is a sound achievement I proposed earlier, but its credit and scope are less settled and it has only one supporter. Any award is preferred to no award.
recusal_note: As WACQT director and a close colleague of Chalmers superconducting-circuit groups, I could face a conflict on circuit QED, but that candidate is not on the final slate. The slate (lattice clocks, IceCube, cold-atom lattices) has no apparent personal connection from my profile.
